text:
Alex Kim: quick sync — thinking through a policy-engine addition: tenant-specific hysteresis + lightweight debug hooks. goal is to reduce 'flip-flop' routing when latency/cost signals bounce during noisy periods.
Maya Patel: yea we've seen that with tiered routes, tenants keep flipping between dedicated and shared pools. hurts cache warmup and kv churn.
Sam R.: can you sketch what the policy surface looks like? curious about backward compat.
Alex Kim: rough idea: add two optional attrs to route rules: `hysteresis_window` (seconds) and `debug_mode` (off|dry_run|log_only). default preserves current behavior.
Priya Singh: `dry_run` seems useful: let us evaluate decisions without enforcing them. how will telemetry show dry-run diffs?
Sam R.: plan: emit both chosen_route and proposed_route in the decision trace when dry_run enabled. tag with `dry_run=true`. then downstream cost/latency calculators ignore enforcement flag.
Maya Patel: also need a small deterministic tie-breaker when signals equal. otherwise hysteresis still leaves ambiguous state. propose `tie_preference` enum: cost|latency|stability. default stability.
Alex Kim: agree. stability -> prefer current active route unless a stronger penalty applies. that reduces churn.
Priya Singh: sample policy snippet for discussion:
```policy
route {
  match tenant == "acme"
  prefer latency < 60ms
  hysteresis_window = 30s
  tie_preference = "stability"
  debug_mode = "dry_run"
}
```
Maya Patel: nice. impl notes: hysteresis_window should be applied per-tenant+route key, persisted in memory for the TTL; when a candidate route crosses threshold, start a timer and only commit if condition holds for full window.
Sam R.: that timer per-key could be a lot. need to bound memory. suggest eviction by LRU + max_entries config and coarse buckets for similar tenants.
Alex Kim: good point. also we should hook into existing decision cache so we don't duplicate state. maybe store hysteresis marks as a small entry alongside route cache with `expires_at`.
Priya Singh: how do we validate correctness? canary plan: 1) unit tests for timer and bucket logic; 2) internal sim with historical trace for 7 days to count flip rate; 3) enable dry_run for 10% of traffic for 48h and compare churn metrics.
Maya Patel: metrics to monitor: route_switch_rate (per-tenant/min), avg_kv_cache_miss_after_switch, p50/p95 latency delta, token_cost_delta. add alert if switch_rate decreases < 30% or latency regresses > 5%.
Sam R.: question about rollbacks: if hysteresis masks a critical capacity drop we could delay fallback. need emergency override: `force_fallback` tag from runtime (ops) that bypasses hysteresis.
Alex Kim: yes we already have an emergency path. ensure `force_fallback` has highest precedence and is visible in traces.
Priya Singh: one more: debug hooks should let us sample the pre/hysteresis decision and ship those to the trace exporter (with sampling param). keep PII out.
Maya Patel: agree. also add a feature-flag gated `hysteresis_beta` that disables for tenants with SLA flag `no_hysteresis_allowed`.
Sam R.: timeline? can we get an RFC follow-up PR this week? I'll volunteer to review the sim harness changes.
Alex Kim: I'll open a PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-engine/pull/1234 with initial impl + tests + sim scripts. target staging canary next Wed.
deploy-bot: deploy status: staged/policy-engine/feature/hysteresis -> build passed ✅, deploy scheduled for 2026-03-25 02:00 UTC
Priya Singh: sweet. action items: Alex open PR (in progress), Sam review sim, Maya add metrics/alerts, I'll draft rollout doc + dry_run query for console.
Maya Patel: also add a small engineering note about memory budget for per-tenant timers (default 50k entries, configurable).
Alex Kim: noted. thanks everyone. leaving thread for updates. :thumbsup:
